631	## Formulas
632	
633	*Conventions.* Every formula below is a **presentation** computation. Nothing here is hashed into `state_hash`, replicated or persisted (KERN D.12 excludes the perceived channel), so the kernel's integer-only determinism rule does not bind D.1 to D.13 and D.15 to D.17, which use floating point on the render thread. **D.14 is the one integer-only formula**: its outputs must reproduce across builds and platforms and are pinned by test vectors (AC-PF-30). Angles are degrees on the instrument's dial arc `arc_deg`; dial readings are per mille (`pm`) of the instrument's range, `pm = deg x 1000 / arc_deg`; pixel measures are art px of the 640x360 grid (`n` art px is `n x k` screen px at ladder step `k`). Time is either **sim time** (`T_c`, the last committed tick count, plus `tick_alpha`, KERN D.3) or **`present_time`** (PIPE PR-9, frozen while PAUSED); each formula says which. `[PLACEHOLDER]` marks a number invented here (range and registered-name proposal in Tuning Knobs); a name followed by "(cited)" is owned elsewhere and used at its registry value. The numbering D.1 to D.17 is the one the rules cite: PF-11 D.1, PF-13 D.2 and D.3, PF-17 D.4, PF-15 D.5, PF-14 D.6, PF-21 D.7, PF-30 D.8, PF-18 D.9, PF-31 D.10, PF-32 D.11, PF-42 D.12, D.13 CPU, PF-37 D.14, PF-20 D.15, PF-35 D.16, PF-19 D.17. Dependency formulas are referenced by name, never restated: KERN D.3 `tick_alpha`, KERN D.10 `rng_derive` (sim-only, never called here), KERN D.12 `state_hash`, PIPE D.15 `flash_count`, PIPE D.16 `D_BUDGET`, LO-22 (including `flash_governor`), SN D.5 (onset). GDScript integer overflow semantics, `Dictionary` ordering and per-call costs are not sourceable (there is no `scripting.md` or `core.md` in `docs/engine-reference/godot/`); every place that depends on them is marked `[UNV]`.
634	
635	### D.1 Lie clock
636	
637	The lie clock formula (registry: `lie_displayed_value`; covers D.1 to D.4) is defined as:
638	
639	`lie_tau = max(0, (T_c - SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR * act_run + tick_alpha) / TICK_RATE)`
640	
641	`first_frame_discrepancy_bound_deg = GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG * (n_f + 1) / TICK_RATE`
642	
643	**Variables:**
644	
645	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
646	|---|---|---|---|---|
647	| `T_c` | int | 0 to 2^53 | KERN tick counter | last committed tick; presentation reads it and never writes |
648	| `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` | int | 12 (cited, registered; equal to the kernel hook divisor by relation, not a knob) | Sanity | ticks per sanity run |
649	| `act_run` | int | >= 0 | `sanity.perception` entry (`active_run` = `start_run` + delay_runs, published by Sanity; registry `sanity.perception`) | the run on which the entry became ACTIVE. Sanity stamps `start_run` at the accept and activates `ONSET_DELAY_RUNS` (10 to 25 runs) later, so `start_run` is **not** the origin. |
650	| `tick_alpha` | float | [0, 1] | KERN D.3 (cited) | interpolation fraction inside the current tick |
651	| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 (cited) | Command & Simulation Layer | ticks per second |
652	| `n_f` | int | 1 to 2 | measured | ticks that elapse per rendered frame (1 at 60 fps, 2 at the 30 fps floor) |
653	| `lie_tau` | float s | 0 to about 120.2 | derived | seconds since activation; the upper end is the `LIE_LIFE_S` maximum (120 s, Sanity) plus one run and one frame |
654	| `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` | float deg/s | 2.0 (named here, value from ART 7.3) | art bible | the fastest drift |
655	
656	**Output Range:** `lie_tau` is 0 at activation and clamped at 0 when a restore or a `force_stage` makes `act_run x 12 > T_c`. It is frozen while PAUSED (the tick and `tick_alpha` are frozen). It is unbounded above only if Sanity fails to remove an expired entry. **First-frame bound:** the first rendered frame sees the entry at most one frame after its hook tick, so `lie_tau <= (n_f + 1) / TICK_RATE` and the displayed-minus-true discrepancy on the first ACTIVE frame is at most `2.0 x 3 / 60 = 0.1 deg` at the 30 fps floor (0.067 deg at 60 fps), which is below `LEAK_EPS_DEG` 0.25 deg: the first frame carries no visible departure (AC-PF-45 tests "below `LEAK_EPS_DEG`", not "exactly zero"). If the Sanity hook's phase offset is not 0, `act_run x 12` is up to 11 ticks (0.18 s) early; the error is constant per lie and invisible.
657	
658	**Example:** `act_run` 1000, `T_c` 12300, `tick_alpha` 0.5: `lie_tau = (12300 - 12000 + 0.5) / 60 = 5.008 s`. A restore that lands with `T_c` 11990 gives `(11990 - 12000 + 0) / 60 < 0`, clamped to 0. While PAUSED for 30 s `T_c` and `tick_alpha` do not move, so `lie_tau` stays 5.008 s.
659	
660	### D.2 Glide parameters (rate and magnitude, drawn once per lie)
661	
662	The glide parameters formula is defined as:
663	
664	`rate_draw = GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG + (GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG - GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG) * (h_rate mod 1001) / 1000`
665	
666	`D_draw = D_DRAW_MIN_DEG + (D_MAX_FRAC_ARC * arc_deg - D_DRAW_MIN_DEG) * (h_mag mod 1001) / 1000` (kind GLIDE); `D_target = D_draw` for GLIDE and `D_target = D_MAX_FRAC_ARC * arc_deg` for FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL, whose needle stops at the zone (D.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
667	
668	`rate_floor = max(GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG, 28.6 / needle_len_px)`
669	
670	`rate_need = D_target / (GLIDE_REACH_FRAC * L_s)`
671	
672	`rate_nom = clamp(max(rate_draw, rate_need), rate_floor, GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG)`
673	
674	`D_eff = min(D_target, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC * rate_nom * L_s)` (independent of `rm` and of the live true value: reduced motion scales the **time axis only**, so it is not a hidden difficulty slider)
675	
676	`rate = max(RM_RATE_FLOOR_DEG, rm * rate_nom)`, `t_arrive = D_eff / rate`
677	
678	**Variables:**
679	
680	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
681	|---|---|---|---|---|
682	| `h_rate`, `h_mag` | uint32 | 0 to 2^32 - 1 | D.14, tags 2 and 3 | per-lie hash draws of `(viewer, ref_key, lie_key, 0)` (`epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw, D.14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
683	| `GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG`, `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` | float deg/s | 0.5, 2.0 (named here, values from ART 7.3) | art bible | the drift-rate band (registry: `GLIDE_RATE_BAND`, with `NEVER_REST_MAX_S` and `WANDER_AMP_PX`; it bounds the **drift** component only; the wander is separate, D.4) |
684	| `D_DRAW_MIN_DEG` | float deg | 24 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 24 to 40 (raised from 12 to 40 so `rm_min x D_DRAW_MIN_DEG >= D_VIS_MIN_DEG` holds across the knob ranges *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*) | Filter | smallest drawn departure |
685	| `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` | float | 0.4 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0.25 to 0.5 | Filter | largest departure as a fraction of the arc |
686	| `arc_deg` | float deg | 180 to 300 (240 used in examples) | calibration record (PF-45, provisional) | dial sweep |
687	| `needle_len_px` | float art px | >= 14.3 (`NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 16, eligibility floor 14.3 = `28.6 / GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`); recommended 24 | calibration record (provisional) | pivot-to-tip length; below 14.3 the needle is ineligible (`28.6 / 14 = 2.04 > GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`) |
688	| `28.6` | float | constant | derived | `0.5 x 180 / pi`: the angular rate that moves the tip 0.5 art px per second |
689	| `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC` | float | 0.6 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0.4 to 0.8 | Filter | fraction of the lie's life by which the departure must complete |
690	| `L_s` | float s | 40 to 120 | `(end_run - act_run) x 0.2` from the entry (the `LIE_LIFE_S` range, SN-16) | remaining life from activation (`end_run` = `active_run` + life_runs, registry `sanity.perception`) |

752	### D.4 Wander and the never-rest bound
753	
754	The wander formula is defined as:
755	
756	`w_px(t_p) = WANDER_AMP_PX * blend_in(lie_tau) * sin(2 * pi * f_w * t_p + phi_w)`, `blend_in(x) = min(1, x / WANDER_ONSET_S)`, applied along the needle's tangent (a unit vector at angle `phi_n` from the x axis) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
757	
758	`w_pm = w_px * 1000 / (needle_len_px * arc_deg * pi / 180)`
759	
760	`f_w = WANDER_F_MIN + (WANDER_F_MAX - WANDER_F_MIN) * (h_wf mod 1001) / 1000`, `phi_w = 2 * pi * (h_wp mod 1000) / 1000`
761	
762	`dwell_max(A, f, phi_n) = acos(1 - 1 / (A * m)) / (pi * f)`, `m = max(abs(cos phi_n), abs(sin phi_n))` (`A * m >= 1`), worst case `m = 1 / sqrt(2)` at 45 degrees, and the assertion `WANDER_AMP_PX / sqrt(2) >= 1 / (1 - cos(pi * WANDER_F_MIN * NEVER_REST_MAX_S))` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
763	
764	**Variables:**
765	
766	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
767	|---|---|---|---|---|
768	| `t_p` | float s | >= 0 | `present_time` (PIPE PR-9) | the wander phase carries no information, so it runs on `present_time` |
769	| `WANDER_AMP_PX` | float art px | 2.2 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 2.1 to 2.6 at `WANDER_F_MIN` 0.40 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Filter | peak excursion of the tip along its tangent; the lower bound is the two-axis assertion above (2.05 at 0.40 Hz) |
770	| `WANDER_F_MIN`, `WANDER_F_MAX` | float Hz | 0.40 and 0.45 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (min range 0.40 to 0.45); max below 0.5 (ART 7.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Filter | frequency band; disjoint from the 6 to 10 Hz tremor |
771	| `WANDER_ONSET_S` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | float s | 1.0 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0.5 to 3.0 | Filter | the wander fades **in** linearly so the first ACTIVE frame has zero offset (D.1) and the onset rest stays short; also `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (PF-8 `tremor_weight_pm`) |
772	| `WANDER_BLEND_S` | float s | 3 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 1 to 6 | Filter | the wander fades **out** from the removal frame (D.6), so a return has no step and CLEAR needs a wander of 0 |
773	| `h_wf`, `h_wp` | uint32 | 0 to 2^32 - 1 | D.14, tags 4 and 5 | per-lie frequency and phase draws |
774	| `NEVER_REST_MAX_S` | float s | 1.0 (cited ceiling, ART 7.3 and SNV-25; not tunable above 1.0) | art bible | the longest the quantised tip may stay on one pixel |
775	| `A`, `f`, `phi_n` | float art px, float Hz, deg | `A` 2.2 default; `f` 0.40 to 0.45; `phi_n` 0 to 90 (by symmetry) | `WANDER_AMP_PX`, `f_w`, the needle's pose | amplitude, frequency and tangent angle in the dwell formula *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
776	
777	**Output Range:** `abs(w_px) <= WANDER_AMP_PX`. **Never-rest proof (held state, two axes)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The tip is drawn at an integer art-px position (nearest sampling) and moves along the needle's tangent, so its rounded position is the pair of two rounded axis positions and it changes when either axis's rounded coordinate changes. Per axis the tip is a sinusoid of amplitude `A m_i` (`m_x = abs(cos phi_n)`, `m_y = abs(sin phi_n)`) about an offset `c_i`, the fractional pixel position of the held target. One axis stays on one pixel longest in the unit-wide level band that sits at the sinusoid's peak with its lower edge exactly at the mean, a fraction `acos(1 - 1/(A m_i)) / pi` of the period, so its dwell is `acos(1 - 1/(A m_i)) / (pi f)`. The pair rests only while both axes rest; the worst case aligns both bands on the same peak, and the dwell is then that of the axis with the *larger* amplitude, `m = max(m_x, m_y)`, which is smallest and so worst at 45 degrees (`m = 1/sqrt(2)`). At `A` 2.0 and 0.35 Hz the single-axis dwell is 0.952 s but the 45-degree dwell is **1.158 s**, over the 1.0 s ceiling, and no amplitude inside the old range (1.85 to 2.5) could fix it (it needs 2.59 px at 0.35 Hz); at `A` 2.2 and `WANDER_F_MIN` 0.40 the dwell is **0.959 s at 45 degrees** (0.791 s at 0 and 90 degrees), a margin of 4 %. A brute-force model over a 24 x 24 grid of fractional offsets and needle angles 0 to 90 degrees in 15-degree steps agrees with the analytic bound to 0.02 s (0.942 s measured at 45 degrees; 0.998 s against 1.001 s analytic at `A` 2.0 and 0.405 Hz, the smallest frequency that would have fixed the old amplitude). The proof is for a **single sinusoid**: the two-sine sum (0.6 and 0.4 weights) proposed in a specialist draft has a beat envelope that falls to 0.2 of its peak, in which the rounded tip rests for the length of a beat, so it is not adopted. Under reduced motion the wander is **not scaled** (PF-39), so `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` does not touch the bound. **Onset (measured, bounded):** during ONSET the drift moves the tip at least 0.5 art px per second by `rate_floor` (tip speed `v = needle_len_px x rate x pi / 180`: 0.50 px/s at 24 px and 1.19 deg/s) and the wander fades in linearly over `WANDER_ONSET_S`; the worst-case rest from the first ACTIVE frame, over needle angle, phase and fractional pixel and with no credit for the drift, is **1.15 s** at 0.40 Hz (1.04 s at 0.45 Hz), inside the stated bound `ONSET_REST_MAX_S` = `WANDER_ONSET_S + NEVER_REST_MAX_S` = 2.0 s (AC-PF-46). A lie whose truth sits at a dial stop (`lie_short_reach`) keeps the full wander, because the target clamp leaves the wander margin `W_M` (D.3), and relies on it as its motion mode.
778	
779	**Example:** `needle_len_px` 24, `arc_deg` 240 (4.19 rad), `WANDER_AMP_PX` 2.2: `w_pm_peak = 2.2 x 1000 / (24 x 4.19) = 21.9 pm` (5.25 deg, 2.2 pixels at the tip). Peak tip speed at 0.45 Hz is `2 pi x 0.45 x 2.2 = 6.22 px/s`, which is 14.9 deg/s angular on a 24-px needle: far above the 0.5 to 2 deg/s band, which is why the band is read as the drift component only (CONFLICT C-1). With hash `H(1, 0x1234, 7, 0)`: `h_wf mod 1001` = 467 gives `f_w = 0.40 + 0.05 x 0.467 = 0.4234 Hz` and `phi_w = 2 pi x 0.105 = 0.66 rad`; the worst-case dwell at 0.4234 Hz is `acos(1 - 1/1.556) / (pi x 0.4234) = 0.906 s` at 45 degrees and 0.746 s at 0 degrees. Assertion at defaults: `2.2 / sqrt(2) = 1.556 >= 1 / (1 - cos(pi x 0.40 x 1.0)) = 1.447` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

920	### D.9 Lying-digit tick schedule

922	The lying-digit tick formula is defined as:
923	
924	`T_tick = max(LIE_TICK_MS, N_r * 334)`
925	
926	`t_k = k * T_tick + j * T_tick / N_r` on `present_time`, `j` the readout's stagger index (ordered by hash tag 6); the stagger spacing `T_tick / N_r` is never below 334 ms, the single-readout floor
927	
928	`q_k = clamp(round(slew_value(t_k) / lsb), q_lo, q_hi)`, `q_lo = round(value_lo / lsb)`, `q_hi = round(value_hi / lsb)`; in TICK mode, if `q_k == q_{k-1}`, `q_k = q_{k-1} + sgn_k` (one `lsb`, sign from hash tag 6, flipped if it would leave `[q_lo, q_hi]`), so the digit changes every tick; in STALE mode `q_k` follows the **displayed** needle value by ticks while the lie is in ONSET and is **held from arrival** (when `delta_pm` reaches its aim), never the zone centre while the needle is still short of it, so the digit does not change while the ship changes. During RETURN the numeral keeps the TICK rule on the returning `slew_value` and switches to the honest grid at CLEAR (PF-18). A region gap governor defers any lying tick due less than 334 ms after the previous lying tick in the region; it never defers an honest swap, and the lying-to-honest switch lands on the next HUD grid boundary (PF-18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

Pause freezes the tick and therefore the lie. Presentation phases that carry no information (wander phase, breath phase, tick cadence) run on `present_time` (PIPE PR-9). The displayed value is a **pure function of the entry, the live true value, `lie_tau` and per-lie constants, modulo PRESENTATION-local state**: the single slew state of PF-13 and PF-14, which is never persisted and is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). While a lie is ACTIVE its displayed value is the formula's value, so a restore reproduces it **up to the slew gap that was still closing at the save** (D.3, PF-33) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the per-lie constants (rate, magnitude, wander frequency and phase, tick stagger and sign, sound-breath period) are restore-exact because their hash key is the saved `lie_id` (in the saved ledger, with its counter `next_lie_id`), and `epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw (D.14); the GLIDE direction and the numeral mode are not hash draws but published entry fields (`direction`, `params.readout_mode`; PF-13, PF-18), saved with the entry *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`, `direction`, `readout_mode`)*. `start_run` and `active_run` are used for the clock only.
299	*Why.* A trajectory on `present_time` would restart from phase 0 after a restore and show a different displayed value (breaking PF-33); a trajectory on sim time is restore-exact and pause-consistent. A lie is a moving value of the world, so it is interpolated with `tick_alpha` (PIPE PR-8 rule 5), not an animation (rule 6): the world moved, so the lie must have advanced. The clock starts at **activation**, not at the accept: Sanity stamps `start_run` at the accept (SN-16, EC-SN-29) and activates `ONSET_DELAY_RUNS` (10 to 25 runs, 2 to 5 s) later, so a clock from `start_run` would put the first ACTIVE frame 2 to 5 s into the glide, a first-frame jump of up to 10 deg that PF-13 and SNV-13 forbid.
300	Sanity publishes `active_run` in the perception entry (registry `sanity.perception`); `act_run` is that field.
301	*Edge notes.* This is the wording the systems-designer proposed for the "pure function" ruling (C-SD2): the lie never snaps (SNV-11), so a step in the true value needs a slew state, and R8's purity holds up to that state. (orchestrator ruling: R8 amended in the live text.)
302	
303	**PF-12. Lie presentation lifecycle** (Sanity's PENDING, ACTIVE, EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED mapped to pixels).
304	
305	| Sanity state | Filter presentation | Notes |
306	|---|---|---|
307	| PENDING | nothing drawn; `perceived` honest | invisible by SN-16; no pre-onset hint |
308	| ACTIVE, onset | ONSET: the displayed value departs the true value on the glide path from displayed-minus-true = 0; the gleam is already at `floor_eff` (D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the sound request is already on | no first-frame jump; the leak is born with the lie |
309	| ACTIVE, arrived | HOLD: the displayed value sits at its false region with wander (PF-17); the leak is steady | never rests |
310	| EXPIRED, DEBUNKED or INVALIDATED (the entry has left `sanity.perception`) | RETURN: a rate-limited follower closes the gap to the live true value at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`; the leak follows the remaining discrepancy through a downward-rate-limited follower (D.5); `lie_id`, `lie_kind` and `leak_modes` stay as they were until CLEAR *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the sound level follows the leak, then off at CLEAR | **presentation-identical for all three end types**; no verdict flash, no relief cue |
311	| **CLEAR** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* = the *later* of three conditions: displayed-minus-true discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.25 deg; range 0.1 to 0.5; registered); gleam amplitude at 0 (D.5); wander faded to 0 (`WANDER_BLEND_S` after removal, D.6) | CLEAR: `motion_mode` returns to HONEST without an event, `lie_id` and `lie_kind` become 0 and NONE on that frame, the sound request goes OFF; honest settle is allowed again | the mode returns without a signal; until CLEAR the record is a RETURN record, so a gleam is never reported on an honest record and a wander is never faded under an honest label |
312	
313	*Rule.* The entry's disappearance from `sanity.perception` is the **only end signal**; the Filter cannot distinguish the three end types and does not try. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Because Sanity lists every ACTIVE entry of the seat whether or not the seat stands in the subject's compartment, marking it with a bool `away` (SN-23), a disappearance can mean only an end (EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED); crossing a hatch, a camera pan or a zoom change never removes or adds an entry and never starts ONSET, RETURN or CLEAR. `away` is read by exactly one Filter consumer, the rim gate via `reach_lie_active` (PF-23, D.7 `gate_RIM`); it is an input to no draw, mode, envelope, S3 state, audio request or counter, and a lint (AC-PF-8) fails any other read. A stage change never ends a lie (SN-16).
314	*Edge notes.* The return track is presentation-local: a restore during RETURN shows the true value from the first frame, behind the black hold; no lie is active then, so it is not a clean-frame oracle (E-PF-5). Sanity does not retain ended entries for `LIE_TAIL_S` (OQ-PF-9 answered: ended entries are not retained, loading clears the tail; registry `sanity.perception`), so the tail record and its restore edge are accepted.
315	
316	**PF-13. Glide laws: GLIDE tracks a discrepancy, FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL target a zone.**
317	*Rule.* Two laws, each a history-free formula of `(lie_tau, live true value, per-lie constants)` (D.3). **GLIDE** (SN-16 kind) is *delta-tracking*: the displayed value is the live true value plus a signed offset that grows along the glide path at the per-lie rate and then holds, so the discrepancy can neither collapse nor grow unseen between Sanity's 5 Hz re-checks. **FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL** are *zone-targeting*: the displayed value departs toward an aim point inside the instrument's OK (or alarm) zone interval at the per-lie rate (the nearest zone point to the true value, pushed `ZONE_MARGIN_PM` inside; success is **the displayed interval, the held value plus the wander, intersecting the zone interval** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*) and then holds the zone, because "OK" is a place on the dial, not an offset; a FALSE_OK that kept tracking a degrading truth would stop hiding it. In both laws the displayed-minus-true discrepancy is 0 at `lie_tau` 0, so there is **no first-frame jump**, and the needle never snaps and never settles. The per-lie **rate** is drawn from the hash (PF-37) inside `[rate_floor, GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG]`, where `GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG` 0.5 and `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` 2.0 are names introduced here, values from ART 7.3 (they are not registry constants), and `rate_floor = max(GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG, 28.6 / needle_len_px)`, where 28.6 is `0.5 x 180 / pi` (the rate that moves the needle tip 0.5 art px per second; PF-17; the per-lie rate and magnitude draw is D.2); the **magnitude** is drawn from the hash and then reduced so the departure completes within `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.6; range 0.4 to 0.8) of the lie's life; it is capped at `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.4; range 0.25 to 0.5) of the dial arc; the dial stop is handled live by clamping the target (D.3), never by shrinking the per-lie magnitude. For FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL the magnitude is the cap itself (the needle stops at the zone, D.3), so a zone inside the cap is reachable whenever the life allows (D.2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `direction`)* Sanity picks the *kind* and the *direction* (L-D; entry field `direction`: 1 COMFORT, 2 ALARM, stored at the accept and immutable for a `lie_id`, since a changed derivation INVALIDATES the lie, SN-16). The Filter never chooses or re-draws a direction. FALSE_OK implies COMFORT and FALSE_FAIL implies ALARM (zone-targeting; a debug-build assertion checks that the entry agrees); a GLIDE's dial side is `s = d x c_dial` (D.3); the Filter picks only the rate and magnitude (SN-23: WHAT and WHEN, never HOW). Invariant: a GLIDE never moves against its published direction (Sanity's rails L-G, L-W and L-S key on `direction`; a COMFORT-ledger lie drawn toward alarm would visibly push a lethal clock the wrong way). Both laws feed **one slew state per ref**, rate-bounded by `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, which keeps the needle from snapping after a step in the true value and closes any residual gap (including the in-flight value of a return, PF-14); wander is added outside the slew (D.3, D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The slew is additionally held within `DISC_CAP_PM` of the true value (D.3): a documented, bounded exception to the no-snap rule that stops a truth step or a fast truth ramp (a breach) from leaving the needle a full dial away from the room, which would break the 40 % fairness cap and hide the emergencies `W_MIN_WARNING_S` protects (OQ-PF-40).

320	
321	**PF-14. Lie end: the glide-return.**
322	*Rule.* On entry removal the Filter starts a return track and moves the displayed value toward the **live** true value at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, default 3.0 deg/s; range 2.0 to 8.0; registered; D.6), never overshooting, never settling, never snapping, and tracking the true value at the same bounded rate if it moves meanwhile. It is identical for EXPIRED, INVALIDATED and DEBUNKED (SN-16). The leak amplitude follows the remaining displayed-minus-true discrepancy (PF-15), so there is no separate "lie over" event; the record stays a RETURN record, with `lie_id` and `lie_kind` non-zero, until CLEAR (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Build assertion: `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`.
323	*Why.* SN-16, SNV-11 and P4 ("no verdict"): the end type must never be an oracle. A return slower than the top glide rate would let a debunked needle outlast a live lie, making DEBUNKED a punishment; a much faster return is a legible "the lie just ended".
324	*Edge notes.* Under reduced motion the glide is scaled by `rm` and the return by `rm_ret = max(rm, RM_RETURN_FLOOR)` (`RM_RETURN_FLOOR` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.83; range 0.8 to 1.0), which caps the reduced-motion return at about 1.2 times the normal return duration (an unbounded slowdown, 1.43 times at `rm` 0.7, was a hidden difficulty cost and a longer tail that marks an ending); the assertion `rm_ret * GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= rm * GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` holds (2.5 >= 1.4 at defaults) (PF-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A new lie on a ref mid-return **starts from its own formula** (discrepancy against the true value is 0 at `lie_tau` 0), never from the return's value, so an ACTIVE lie's displayed value never depends on presentation-local return state. The slew of PF-13 closes the residual gap from the in-flight return value at a rate of at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`: no snap, a history-free law, and after a restore the displayed value equals the formula from the first frame (E-PF-3).
325	
326	**PF-15. The leak triple, the ACTIVE floor and the drop rule.**
327	*Rule.* Each lie renders its entry's `leak_modes`: GLEAM (the violet gleam), GLIDE (the motion signature) and SOUND (the sound signature), each sufficient on its own (HR-5). While a lie is ACTIVE its gleam amplitude is never below the stage-indexed floor `floor_eff` (D.5: `AMP_FLOOR_PM` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 400 per mille at stages 0 to 1, falling to `AMP_FLOOR_S3_PM` 250 at stage 3; range 250 to 600) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* even at zero discrepancy, and above that it follows the discrepancy (its rises are instantaneous, its falls are limited to `R_AMP_ACT`, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; after the entry leaves it follows the *remaining* discrepancy from the amplitude at removal, with no step (D.5). The sound request is emitted on the first ACTIVE frame, not when the needle has visibly moved. **Mandatory modes and the drop rule (SN-15 L-L made computable; P1 sane-palette rule).** Two modes are **mandatory on every lie and never droppable**: **GLEAM**, the *palette mode*, because P1 requires that "every hallucination leaks [flesh and violet] somewhere ... Subtle is allowed; absent is not", and a glide or a sound is not a palette leak (a lie drawn with motion and sound but no violet anywhere would be a palette-silent lie); and the **motion mode** (the one mode that survives both hue removal and mute). A lie whose violet is carried by a draw other than the host gleam (a SPRITE_SWAP frame whose gleam leads the cut, a VS-A lure whose flesh or violet content is its own leak, a class-(c) or phantom rig contour with `leak` above 0, E-PF-37) satisfies the palette mode through that draw, and its entry still carries the GLEAM bit. **Only SOUND may be dropped:** at stage 2 or 3, only when the entry carries all three, only when it is not the first lie, chosen by a PRESENTATION-only hash test against `MODE_DROP_PM` and counted in `leak_modes_dropped`. By construction `leak_modes` therefore always contains GLEAM and the motion mode on every ACTIVE lie (`popcount >= 2`, `leak_modes & GLEAM != 0`), at every stage and every level of detail. This is a lint as well as a runtime rule: `lint_leak_palette.gd` (AC-PF-18) fails the build if any lie-content row, fixture or drop-rule branch can produce an ACTIVE lie with `leak_modes & GLEAM == 0`. `MODE_DROP_PM` is `[PLACEHOLDER]` **0 at MVP** (lint) (shipped value; `first_lie` is now supplied).
328	**The invariant, restated: GLEAM plus at least one hue-independent motion mode, on every ACTIVE lie, on every fallback path** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The motion mode is the one that survives hue removal *and* mute, so SOUND never counts as it. Every corruptible surface class has a named motion mode, in the table below; a lie on a surface for which no motion mode can be drawn, or whose gleam cannot be drawn within the budget (PF-42), is **not drawn at all** (the honest path, counter `lie_unrenderable`). The Filter never draws a lie with only part of the pair, so a fallback can reduce how many lies are drawn and never how a drawn lie leaks. `lint_leak_palette.gd` (AC-PF-18) and the fallback lint (AC-PF-108) fail the build for any branch that can.
329	
330	| Surface class | Lie kinds | Hue-independent motion mode (`motion_mode`) | Notes |
331	|---|---|---|---|
332	| Dial gauge needle (GRAPH_NODE, GRAPH_COMPARTMENT, SUIT_KEY dial) | GLIDE, FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | needle drift plus the never-rest wander (record mode GLIDE, or STALE for FALSE_*); the card numeral adds TICK or STALE | the wander runs in every needle lie, including one whose truth sits at a dial stop (D.3 live clamp, E-PF-10); a needle shorter than `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` is not lied on unless the ref has a visible digit mechanism (E-PF-11) |
333	| Linear sight-glass | same | meniscus drift plus the wander (PF-45 linear branch) | below `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` not lied on |
334	| Numeral-only readout (digit mechanism, no needle) | GLIDE; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | TICK for GLIDE; for FALSE_* STALE **plus the gleam breath** (a held digit alone is not motion, so the record carries BREATH's gleam modulation) | D.9 |
335	| State glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state (static pair) | SPRITE_SWAP; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL on a housing appearance frame | BREATH: the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s (D.8; HR-7 already treats the breath as a fringe's hue-independent channel) | the false frame itself is static; E-PF-12 |
336	| Machine sprite, continuous frame (rotor on a stopped machine) | SPRITE_SWAP | the rotor cadence drift (record mode GLIDE, D.17) | |
337	
338	*Why.* "Subtle is allowed; absent is not" (ART:73). The earlier draft let the hash choose *which* of the three modes to drop, so a stage-2 or stage-3 lie could have been drawn as glide plus sound with no violet anywhere, breaking the pillar's sane-palette clause (creative-director concern, CD-GDD-ALIGN); the palette mode is now mandatory exactly as the motion mode already was. The stage-2 rim fringe and the stage-3 hue bleed are not relied on to cover a gap, because both are conditional and cuttable. A leak that is a pure function of discrepancy is 0 on the first frame, which would break SN-15 L-L ("the first lie carries all three") and SNV-13 ("full leak from frame one"); the floor closes that onset hole. The `AMP_FLOOR_PM` visibility floor is a sibling of `DECOY_LEAK_ALPHA_PM` 300 and `BREATH_FLOOR_PM` 400 at stages 0 to 2 (the gleam floor is 400 and 325); at stage 3 the user-ruled floor of 250 (D74) deliberately sits below the decoy's 300 (a VS-A overlay, absent at MVP), and the alignment is routed to Lighting and the art-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
339	*Edge notes.* A malformed entry with empty `leak_modes`, or with a non-empty `leak_modes` that lacks the GLEAM bit, is a debug-build assertion; release draws GLEAM and GLIDE for the empty entry, **adds GLEAM** to the other, and counts `leak_repaired`, so a palette-silent lie is never drawn (E-PF-49). If audio is muted or unavailable the lie keeps two modes; the player's mute is not a Filter event.
340	
341	**PF-16. The gleam.**
342	*Rule.* Violet `#B07BE6` (never the core `#8A3FD1`), at an **edge only** (glass edge, needle leading edge, housing edge, sprite contour), never a fill or a plane, `GLEAM_EDGE_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (range 1 to 2), set per rung by Instruments' `gleam_edge_px`: 2 art px at k = 1 and 1 art px at k >= 2, so the gleam is at least 2 screen px at every rung (`GLEAM_EDGE_SCREEN_MIN` 2, OQ-IW-4 accepted inside this range). It is drawn on the corruptible element itself, **lit with its host** (it appears only where the instrument is visible; no lit-gate query is needed and none is made, IA-13), and its amplitude is the PF-15 amplitude (breathing on the static-pair classes, D.5). Its transport is the ladder of PF-42 (instance parameters, then a MultiMesh overlay, else the surface is not lied on); a MultiMesh path must keep the gleam lit with its host and sample the host's `_msk` edge slice, which is spike S-1c *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Its peak channel is capped at `LEAK_MAX_CH`, defined **by relation** as `LEAK_MAX_CH := DECOY_MAX_CH` (0.85, itself at most 0.9 x `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`; `DECOY_MAX_CH` is registered and owned by Lighting; `LEAK_MAX_CH` is a name introduced here for the registry stage, not a knob and not a second value), so a leak never blooms (glow is processed before tonemapping since 4.6) and never reads as a light.
343	*Why.* A gleam on an unlit instrument would be a location oracle and would put a phantom in the dark (SN:1267). The cost of the lit choice is that the on-screen colour shifts under the Tungsten beam (the blue channel is attenuated about a third), which the art-director must accept (OQ-PF-6); the hue-removed test (AC-SN-154) is unaffected.
344	*Edge notes.* On a HUD-layer reading (VS-A) the HUD draws the gleam on its own glass, in HUD px, from `leak_amplitude_pm` and `leak_modes`; the inspect card's glass is drawn by its owning node the same way (Instruments IW-16, with the HUD's gleam helper). The Filter supplies parameters and owns no HUD node (C-3 and OQ-PF-11 closed from the HUD side, OQ-HS-16). `LEAK_MAX_CH` is a **linear** channel value, compared in the same space as `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD` (pre-tonemap), and applies on every surface the Filter parameterises, world layer and HUD-layer glass alike; if HDR output is enabled on the root viewport the cap is re-tested (OQ-HS-13; `[UNV]` until the Lighting spike confirms the colour space of `DECOY_MAX_CH`).
345	
346	**PF-17. Motion signatures and the never-rest rule.**
347	*Rule.* Exactly three motion signatures exist and only one belongs to a lie: **settle** (damped spring, ease-out 250 to 400 ms, overshoot at most 5 %, then still), **tremor** (+-1 art px (+-2 art px at k = 1, so it stays at least 2 screen px; Instruments' `tremor_offset`), irregular, 6 to 10 Hz, around a *true* value) and **glide** (the lie). A lie never borrows settle or tremor; an honest gauge never glides; the returned `motion_mode` is the only switch. The leak's own HR-7 breath (D.8) is a modulation of the gleam and not a fourth gait: it is the motion mode of the static-pair classes (PF-15 table) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Never-rest:** the 0.5 to 2 deg/s band of ART 7.3 bounds the *drift* component only; a separate **wander**, one sinusoid per lie, of `WANDER_AMP_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (2.2 art px at the needle tip, along the needle's tangent; range 2.1 to 2.6 at `WANDER_F_MIN` 0.40, the lower bound being derived in D.4 for the worst needle angle; the art-director's floor of 1 px is met with margin) at a hashed frequency in `WANDER_F_MIN` to `WANDER_F_MAX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.40 to 0.45 Hz; below the 0.5 Hz cap, and disjoint from the 6 to 10 Hz tremor) carries "never rests" for a held lie. (orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's two-sine sum is not adopted, because its beat envelope falls to 0.2 of the peak and the rounded tip would then rest; D.4.) A held lie's tip changes its quantised pixel position at least every `NEVER_REST_MAX_S`, a **cited ceiling of 1.0 s** (ART 7.3 and SNV-25: "the needle is always a pixel from where it was a second ago"; not tunable above 1.0 s), proven in D.4 **on two axes** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the tip moves along the needle's tangent, so at tangent angle `phi` the rounded tip position is a pair of rounded axis positions, and the worst-case dwell on one pixel is `acos(1 - 1/(A m)) / (pi f)` with `m = max(abs(cos phi), abs(sin phi))`, at least `1/sqrt(2)`: the worst needle angle is 45 degrees, where each axis sees only `A / sqrt(2)`. The single-axis figure of the earlier draft (0.952 s at 2.0 px and 0.35 Hz) hid a **1.16 s rest at 45 degrees**, over the art bible's 1.0 s ceiling, which no amplitude inside the old range could fix; so `WANDER_F_MIN` is **0.40 Hz** (range 0.40 to 0.45) and `WANDER_AMP_PX` 2.2 (worst case 0.96 s at 45 degrees, 0.79 s at 0 and 90 degrees). Lie-capable in-world gauges ship a needle of at least 16 art px (recommended 24); a needle shorter than `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 16; range 14.3 to 32; eligibility floor 14.3 = 28.6 / `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`; owner In-World Instruments, provisional) is ineligible for a needle glide **and the surface is not lied on at all** (E-PF-11: a gleam with a sound has no hue-independent motion mode), unless the same ref has a visible digit mechanism whose TICK, or STALE with the gleam breath, is then its motion mode *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

520	### States and Transitions
521	
522	The Filter has no simulation state machine. These are *presentation-local* machines, none persisted, none in `state_hash`; each is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). "Who may cause" names the only actors that can move a machine; the Filter itself never causes a SIM transition.
523	
524	#### S1. Filter service (per client)
525	
526	| State | Entry condition | Exit condition | Behaviour | Who may cause the transition |
527	|---|---|---|---|---|
528	| `COLD` | boot | LOADING begins | no effects; every `perceived` call returns the honest record; the container slot is null | process start |
529	| `HARD_START` | the first RUNNING frame after LOADING; any `force_stage` or `force_level` | one rendered frame later | envelopes set to their targets; every ACTIVE lie drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak; anchors and phases initialised; counter `first_frame_filtered` | Save/Load (LOADING to RUNNING, kernel state); Sanity's QA flags (`force_stage`, `force_level`, SN-28) |
530	| `LIVE` | after `HARD_START` | PAUSED or LOADING | ramps, trajectories, breaths and counters run on their clocks | automatic |
531	| `PAUSED` | kernel pause | resume, or LOADING | `present_time` and the tick are frozen, so every lie clock, ramp, breath, wander and tick freezes; the paused frame still contains every active leak (hue and edge presence do not depend on motion) | the player (pause), the kernel control plane |
532	| `CLEARED` | LOADING, session teardown | `COLD`, then `HARD_START` | presentation-local state (return tracks, slew limiters, envelopes) dropped, never saved | Save/Load, session teardown |
533	
534	#### S2. Stage-bound effect envelope (per viewer, per effect `e` in {rim, bleed, floor}; the class-(c) outline uses `TELL_RAMP_S` in the same form)
535	
536	| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
537	|---|---|---|---|
538	| `OFF` | target 0 and envelope 0 | target > 0 -> `RAMP_UP` | `sanity_view.stage` crossing `STAGE_ENTER` (SIM, instant); for the rim in LIE_BOUND mode (the default) Sanity's `reach_lie_active(P)` becoming true (stage >= 2 and a listed entry with `away` false, `reach_tier` 2 and stepped PENDING to ACTIVE: an ACTIVE lie on a state glyph or lamp-housing glow sprite in the seat's current compartment; a machine-frame lie and any away lie do not drive it; PF-23) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the bleed never leaves `OFF` while `AMBIENT_FRINGES_ENABLED` is false *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
539	| `RAMP_UP` | envelope below target | slews at the rate latched at the target change (`rate_s`, D.7; at most `1/STAGE_RAMP_S`), so every transition lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`; reaching target -> `STEADY`; target drops -> `RAMP_DOWN` | the stage, then `present_time` |
540	| `STEADY` | envelope equals target | target changes -> `RAMP_UP` or `RAMP_DOWN` | the stage |
541	| `RAMP_DOWN` | envelope above target | slews at a rate re-latched at the target change (D.7), so it too lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`; reaching 0 -> `OFF` | the stage (hysteresis exit above `STAGE_ENTER` + `STAGE_HYST` 2000 mSU, after `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25) |
542	
543	The SIM stage steps instantly; the picture arrives like weather. A reversal mid-ramp continues from the current value with its rate re-latched, so the return takes `STAGE_RAMP_S` from any value (D.7). Entering `HARD_START` sets the envelope to its target. The hash `epoch` of the effect increments only in `OFF`.
544	
545	#### S3. Lie presentation (per viewer, per `lie_id`)
546	
547	| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
548	|---|---|---|---|
549	| `NONE` | no entry for the ref and no RETURN in progress, or CLEAR reached after a return (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | entry appears ACTIVE -> `ONSET` | Sanity (entry appears in `sanity.perception`, SN-16) |
550	| `ONSET` | entry ACTIVE and the departure not complete (`lie_tau` below arrival time) | departure complete -> `HOLD`; entry removed early -> `RETURN` (the follower starts from the in-flight discrepancy) | Sanity (removal: expiry, a falsification, an invalidating re-check, a class disable); sim time (arrival) |
551	| `HOLD` | entry ACTIVE and arrived | entry removed -> `RETURN` | Sanity |
552	| `RETURN` | entry absent and CLEAR not yet reached (CLEAR is the later of discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, gleam amplitude 0 and wander faded to 0; `lie_id` and `lie_kind` stay non-zero throughout; the return is the slew state of PF-13 with the live true value as its target, rate `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | CLEAR -> `NONE`; a new entry on the same ref -> `ONSET` **from its own formula** (discrepancy 0 at `lie_tau` 0); the slew closes the gap from the in-flight value at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, no snap (E-PF-3) | the follower at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (presentation); Sanity (a new entry) |
553	
554	`ONSET` and `HOLD` are both `motion_mode` GLIDE (or TICK or STALE for a readout, or BREATH for a static-pair frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); `RETURN` is `motion_mode` RETURN until CLEAR. SPRITE_SWAP uses the same four states with the gleam-leads-cut onset and the type-split return of PF-19. The leak amplitude follows PF-15 in every state; a stage change never moves the machine.
555	
556	#### S4. Class (c) per subject seat B as seen by viewer A (VS-B; MVP stub)
557	
558	| State | Condition | Draw | Who may cause |
559	|---|---|---|---|
560	| `HUMAN` | `harm_eligible(A)` clear and `tell_on(B)` clear | untouched | SIM (Sanity's flags) |
561	| `TELL` | `tell_on(B)` set (shown to A whatever A's own `tell_on`) | outline fringe ramped in by `TELL_RAMP_S`, breathing | Sanity (`tell_on` of B, `SAN_TELL_ON`/`SAN_TELL_OFF` hysteresis), replicated as `SHARED_SUMMARY` |
562	| `RIG` | `harm_eligible(A)` set | horror rig substituted, hard cut, true position, velocity, beam and voice; the fringe, if `tell_on(B)`, is the single leak fringe | Sanity (`harm_eligible` of A: the actor's own SIM bit, `SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS` 150 to set, immediate clear) |
563	| `TELL_AND_RIG` | both | one fringe (SNV-17), never double | both of the above |
564	
565	A is never shown a fringe on A's own body in any state (ART 5.5 read as "never on one's own body"; the own-cone rim fringe sits on the beam rim).
566	
567	#### S5. Mask route
568	
569	| State | Meaning | Transition | Who may cause |
570	|---|---|---|---|
571	| `PER_ELEMENT` (container `NOT_USED`) | MVP: every effect is a per-element material; the container slot is null; not a fault | `CONTAINER_MASKED` after the Vertical Slice spike and its ADR | a project decision (ADR), the pipeline root (slot assignment) |
572	| `CONTAINER_MASKED` | VS-A: a whole-image pass for warm drift on non-anchor content, truth-masked | the mask cannot be exact or allocation fails -> `NONE_C` | the pipeline root; mask availability |
573	| `NONE_C` | fallback: no whole-image pass; per-element only | n/a | mask failure |
574	
575	A null container never reads `NO_MASK` while `filter_route` is `PER_ELEMENT` (PF-25).

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-75c; Detailed Rules PF-18 'Honest-swap accounting'; D.9; OQ-PF-44; sibling hud-and-suit-layer.md HS L316 (GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS)
findings.finding: AC-PF-75c cannot pass at the STRICT default, and this is carried for a third review. The AC says: 'the sum of lying and honest transitions in any rolling second is at most 3, every honest swap that the window cannot hold is skipped to its next grid boundary by the HUD arbiter'. The HUD's rule constant GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1 ('a boundary is never skipped twice in a row ... admitted and counted whatever waits') forces an admission about once per second. At N_r = 3 the lying ticks already run at 2.994/s. Some rolling second therefore holds 4 transitions and the AC's own sum bound fails. The HUD records HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN and leaves it as an ASK to the Filter. OQ-PF-44 'Accept' does not close it.
findings.fix: Rewrite the AC to the achievable oracle. GIVEN STRICT, N_r = 3 lying readouts plus 1 honest numeral in one region, over 60 s: (a) lying ticks 334 +- 1 ms apart, never deferred; (b) the HUD skips at most 1 consecutive honest boundary (GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1), so honest swaps appear at least every 1000 ms; (c) the rolling-second total is at most 3 on every window with no honest swap, and on windows that contain a forced honest swap it is at most 4, each logged as HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN; (d) under the weighted unit ceil(n/2) every window is at most 3. Alternatively cap N_r at 2 in STRICT. Record the choice in OQ-PF-44 and in the HUD's AC-HS-140/141.

findings.section: Formulas D.5 (Output Range, L817), D.11 (L1001), Detailed Rules L443 and PF-15; AC-PF-19, AC-PF-81
findings.finding: The claim that the only amplitude discontinuity is the rise-only onset step is false by the file's own formula. This is the most pillar-relevant carry (third pass), and the text at L443, L817 and L1001 is unchanged. D.5 says 'rises stay instantaneous because they follow the glide, slope at most 61 pm/s'. But disc = |slew_pm - u_true| and the slew lags a truth step. Vector: GLIDE lie at disc 10 deg (amp 696). The truth steps 20 deg against the offset (a repair, a valve). On the next frame disc = 30 deg, g = 1 and a_cand = 1000, so amp rises by 304 pm in one frame. From disc about 0 (floor 400) the jump is 600 pm, which is Y_v x 0.6 = 0.175 of relative luminance, with no fall limiter. The gleam therefore brightens on exactly the frame the true value moves. That is the 'truth just moved' oracle the CD said must not ship. AC-PF-19 even asserts 'a rise is instantaneous'. Flash safety still holds (single direction, followed by a limited fall), so this is an oracle and a false claim, not a safety defect.
findings.fix: Rate-limit the ACTIVE rise as well. Use a_env(t+dt) = clamp(a_cand, a_env - R_AMP_ACT*dt, a_env + R_RISE*dt) with R_RISE of about 120 pm/s. That is above the 61 pm/s glide slope, so a normal glide is unaffected. It keeps the onset step the one intentional jump, and hard_start still sets a_env := a_cand. Then fix L443, L817, L1001, PF-15, AC-PF-19 ('a rise is instantaneous') and AC-PF-81 to match, and add a vector: disc 10 -> 30 deg in one frame gives amp 696 -> 1000 over at least 2.5 s with no per-frame rise above R_RISE*dt. If the oracle is accepted instead, delete the 'only discontinuity' sentences and add the truth-step rise to the accepted-tells list.

findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-34 (L452) and PF-20; Formulas D.5 hard_start, D.8, D.15; AC-PF-66, 66b, 66c, 67
findings.finding: What disc, a_env and amp_snd do while a lying surface is off screen or away is still undefined, and the re-entry rule contradicts the new 'no oracle' ACs. PF-34 says that on the first drawn frame after an off-screen interval the slew is re-latched with hard_start. D.5 defines hard_start as a_env := a_cand, and D.8 resets the gleam breath phi := 0. The sound request stays ON off screen (PF-34, AC-PF-67) and LEVEL = amp_snd = a_env. If a_env was still decaying or was not advanced while off screen, re-entry steps LEVEL by up to 600 pm. That is an audible event that depends on camera movement. AC-PF-67's 'identical capture sequence of amp and sound requests' (away true vs false) can then fail.
findings.fix: State one rule: a_env, disc and amp_snd for a lie off screen or away are advanced by scalar arithmetic on elapsed time, the same way the RETURN follower is (the closed form of the clamped follower; no draw work). Use hard_start only after LOADING or force_stage, never for an off-screen interval. Keep the breath phase on present_time, or latch it analytically. Add to AC-PF-67 a vector: a truth step while off screen, re-entry after 10 s, and LEVEL changes by at most R_AMP_ACT*dt per frame across re-entry.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-66c
findings.finding: AC-PF-66c is not testable as written. It says: 'S3 is NONE or exactly at the follower's elapsed-time position (min(gap, R_ret x elapsed) closed), never restarted from the HOLD value'. 'NONE or exactly at' is a disjunction with no numeric oracle, and gap is not defined for an off-screen lie.
findings.fix: Rewrite: GIVEN a GLIDE lie in HOLD with disc_end 100 pm (24 deg), rm 1.0 (R_ret 12.5 pm/s), the surface off screen or away when end_run passes, and E = 5 s off screen, WHEN next drawn THEN slew_pm = u_true + s*max(0, 100 - 12.5*E) +- 1 pm (= u_true + s*37.5), amp equals the D.5 RETURN value at t_ret = 5 s, and S3 = RETURN. For E >= 8 s (gap 0, wander faded at t_ret >= 3 s) S3 = NONE and lie_id = 0 on that frame. State the vector for both E = 5 s and E = 50 s.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-12; Formulas D.11(a); Tuning 'Derived constraints' row dY_region; OQ-PF-45; Detailed Rules PF-34 / PF-G9
findings.finding: AC-PF-12 mixes pre-cap and post-cap figures, and the zoom toggle is still there. (1) AC-PF-12 and the Derived-constraints row both report 0.0725 at 640x360 k = 3 against a 0.05 'after the cap' bound, then carve out an exemption. After the cap evaluates to 0 breathing gleams the remaining sum is (353.4 + 120) x 0.291 / 2844 = 0.0484, which is at most 0.05. The exemption is unnecessary and the assertion (r) as worded would fail boot at defaults. (2) On a 640x360 window at stage 3 with the rim, N_G_REGION = 0, so a static-pair lie takes the honest path with filter_draws_dropped when the player zooms in to k = 3 and returns when they zoom out. Zoom is therefore a lie detector, which conflicts with PF-G9 and the user's zoom in/out ruling.
findings.fix: (1) State the post-cap value 0.0484 in AC-PF-12 and in the Derived-constraints row, report 0.0725 as 'pre-cap, not asserted', and drop the exemption clause. (2) Do not tie the honest-path fallback to the current k. Either evaluate N_G_REGION at the worst rung of the window's ladder once per lie at activation and hold it for the lie's life, or (preferred, the Pipeline's call) cap the ladder at k_auto + 1 below a 1280x720 window (OQ-PF-45). Add an AC: zoom k = 1 -> 3 -> 1 on 640x360 never changes the drawn lie set.

findings.section: Sibling sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md SN-23 (L357) and Interactions (L1569) vs Filter PF-15 / PF-37 / AC-PF-93
findings.finding: The SOUND-bit drop has two owners and the sibling contradicts the Filter's lint. Sanity still says the drop is 'a pure rng_derive keyed "filter.leak/<PlayerId>/<lie_id>" ... a proposed registry stream', and that the Filter 'owns the SOUND-bit plausibility drop as a pure rng_derive'. The Filter forbids rng_derive (D.14: 'Never rng_derive'; AC-PF-93 lints the source for it) and uses the PRESENTATION hash test against MODE_DROP_PM (tag 7). It is dormant, since MODE_DROP_PM is 0 at MVP, but the two GDDs give opposite implementation instructions. This is carried for a second pass; Sanity was not edited for it.
findings.fix: Under G1 the Filter owns the draw. In Sanity L357 and L1569, replace 'rng_derive keyed filter.leak/...' with 'a Filter-owned presentation hash draw (Perception Filter D.14 tag 7, keyed on the saved lie_id); no kernel stream, no counter, no ledger field'. Drop the 'proposed registry stream' wording.

findings.section: Open Questions OQ-PF-38 item 3; sibling Sanity SN-23 gate (b) (L357)
findings.finding: Sanity's zone-edge eligibility gate is a flat 'zone-edge distance + m_z <= D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000' (400 pm). The Filter can only deliver min(400, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg) = 200 pm at L_s 40 s and 240 deg (D.2: D_eff = min(96, 48) deg). A FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL lie whose zone is 201-400 pm away on a 40-60 s life passes Sanity's gate and then stops short, giving lies_zone_missed. The Filter's own AC-PF-81 labels such a lie 'a weak lie that Sanity's gate should have refused'. OQ-PF-38 still says 'provisional contract until the Filter confirms the constants', but the Filter confirmed them and the derived reach was never handed over.
findings.fix: Edit Sanity gate (b) to use the Filter's published reach: zone-edge distance + m_z <= min(D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg) (200 pm at 40 s, 400 pm from 80 s), with L_s known at the accept. Have the Filter expose reach_pm(L_s, arc_deg) as a pure helper. Then remove the 'provisional' wording in OQ-PF-38 item 3 and add a Sanity AC: a 40 s FALSE_OK whose zone is 250 pm away is refused without a draw.

findings.section: Sibling hud-and-suit-layer.md (HS-28 L257, L1666, AC-HS-104 L1815) and in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md (L398, L985-L998); Open Questions OQ-PF-42
findings.finding: RM_GLIDE_SCALE is still 0.6 in both siblings, against the owner value 0.7 (registry reduced_motion_glide_pm default 700, range 700-1000; Filter L691, L1301). HUD HS-28 and L1666 say '0.6 ... unregistered ... range 0.5-1.0'. AC-HS-104 expects a 2.0 deg/s glide to drop to 1.2 deg/s, but the correct value is 1.4 deg/s, so the test would fail a correct build. Instruments' reduced-motion lint (T_digit / 0.6, 'P 3.05 + 1.34 s') uses the stale divisor; the true figure is smaller, so the lint stays conservative but its worked numbers are wrong. OQ-PF-42 still says 'this GDD edits none of them', which is out of date under G6, and 'HUD has no tremor_weight_pm or BREATH', which is moot for the HUD (it states no tremor on suit readings).
findings.fix: Under G1 the Filter wins. HUD: change 0.6 to 0.7 (registered, range 0.7-1.0, PF-39) at HS-28, L1666 and AC-HS-104 (expected 1.4 deg/s). Instruments: replace 0.6 with 0.7 and recompute the P and p_o2 reduced-motion sums. Close OQ-PF-42 in the Filter, noting that HUD needs neither tremor_weight_pm nor BREATH. After the edits, grep referenced_by documents for RM_GLIDE_SCALE, as the project's consistency-check rule requires.

findings.section: Formulas D.3 (the s latch) and AC-PF-120
findings.finding: If a record holds more than one alarm interval, A is chosen as the interval whose nearest edge is closest to the live u_true at the latch frame (the first listed frame or hard_start). So s depends on live truth and is not restore-exact, yet AC-PF-120 asserts 's is identical after a save/restore'. It is dormant at MVP (dials hold one alarm interval) but the AC is not true for a lie_targets row with two.
findings.fix: Choose A from the static record only, for example the alarm interval nearest mid(OK), so s = d x sgn(mid(OK) - mid(A)) is a function of the entry and the record. Or scope AC-PF-120 to single-alarm records and add a build assertion that MVP records have exactly one.

findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-9 (L277) and Interactions intro (L579, L587)

SN-16's lit-entry rule)', but L279-L285 now define the join on {stable_id, surface} with the IW-8 record. The I-A/I-B intro (L579) still says 'no GDD file existed when this GDD was written ... (provisional) marks every neighbour with no GDD', and L587 quotes Lighting's row as 'undesigned, provisional'.
findings.fix: PF-9: replace the sentence with 'A ref resolves to Sanity's subject_ref {stable_id, surface} through the instrument record found by stable_id (L279)'. Intro: reword to say '(provisional)' now marks only Accessibility Settings and Co-op Session.

findings.section: Edge Cases E-PF-57 (L1244), Formulas D.6 rm row (L848), Cross-References X-3 header (L1788)

(1) E-PF-57 says the boot check fails when 'LEAK_D_FULL_DEG [is] at or below LEAK_EPS_DEG', but AC-PF-49(g) and the Tuning table use '<= 2 x LEAK_EPS_DEG' (the D.5 branch). findings.section: Formulas D.6 Output Range (L855) and Example (L857)
findings.finding: Two reduced-motion figures use 2.5 deg/s where rm_ret x 3 = 0.83 x 3 = 2.49 deg/s: t_return 'at rm 0.7: 38.4 s' (96 / 2.49 = 38.6 s) and the 60-deg example 'rm_ret 0.83 gives 2.5 deg/s ... 24.0 s' (24.1 s). The rate row says 'rm_ret 0.83' but quotes the rounded rate.
findings.fix: Quote 38.6 s and 24.1 s, or state that 0.83 is rounded and the figures use 2.5.

findings.section: Formulas D.10 example table, D.11, AC-PF-12 vs R12 RM-DECK
findings.finding: R12 names RM-DECK as a Steam Deck LCD at 1280x800, but D.10, D.11 and AC-PF-12 label 1280x720 as 'Steam Deck class'. 1280x720 gives the smaller region (A_region_min 6400 vs 7111 at 800), so it is the conservative case, but the labels read as a different machine.
findings.fix: Relabel the 1280x720 rows 'smallest field on RM-DECK (720p letterbox, conservative)', or add an 800-line row (k_auto 2, ladder 1-4, A_region_min 1280 x 800 / (9 x 16) = 7111).

From disc about 0 (floor 400) the jump is 600 pm, which is Y_v x 0.6 = 0.175 of relative luminance, with no fall limiter. The gleam therefore brightens on exactly the frame the true value moves. That is the 'truth just moved' oracle the CD said must not ship. AC-PF-19 even asserts 'a rise is instantaneous'. That is above the 61 pm/s glide slope, so a normal glide is unaffected. It keeps the onset step the one intentional jump, and hard_start still sets a_env := a_cand. findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-34 (L452) and PF-20; Formulas D.5 hard_start, D.8, D.15; AC-PF-66, 66b, 66c, 67
findings.finding: What disc, a_env and amp_snd do while a lying surface is off screen or away is still undefined, and the re-entry rule contradicts the new 'no oracle' ACs. PF-34 says that on the first drawn frame after an off-screen interval the slew is re-latched with hard_start. D.5 defines hard_start as a_env := a_cand, and D.8 resets the gleam breath phi := 0. The sound request stays ON off screen (PF-34, AC-PF-67) and LEVEL = amp_snd = a_env. If a_env was still decaying or was not advanced while off screen, re-entry steps LEVEL by up to 600 pm. That is an audible event that depends on camera movement. AC-PF-67's 'identical capture sequence of amp and sound requests' (away true vs false) can then fail.
findings.fix: State one rule: a_env, disc and amp_snd for a lie off screen or away are advanced by scalar arithmetic on elapsed time, the same way the RETURN follower is (the closed form of the clamped follower; no draw work). Use hard_start only after LOADING or force_stage, never for an off-screen interval. Keep the breath phase on present_time, or latch it analytically. Add to AC-PF-67 a vector: a truth step while off screen, re-entry after 10 s, and LEVEL changes by at most R_AMP_ACT*dt per frame across re-entry.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-66c
findings.finding: AC-PF-66c is not testable as written. It says: 'S3 is NONE or exactly at the follower's elapsed-time position (min(gap, R_ret x elapsed) closed), never restarted from the HOLD value'. 'NONE or exactly at' is a disjunction with no numeric oracle, and gap is not defined for an off-screen lie.
findings.fix: Rewrite: GIVEN a GLIDE lie in HOLD with disc_end 100 pm (24 deg), rm 1.0 (R_ret 12.5 pm/s), the surface off screen or away when end_run passes, and E = 5 s off screen, WHEN next drawn THEN slew_pm = u_true + s*max(0, 100 - 12.5*E) +- 1 pm (= u_true + s*37.5), amp equals the D.5 RETURN value at t_ret = 5 s, and S3 = RETURN. For E >= 8 s (gap 0, wander faded at t_ret >= 3 s) S3 = NONE and lie_id = 0 on that frame. State the vector for both E = 5 s and E = 50 s.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-12; Formulas D.11(a); Tuning 'Derived constraints' row dY_region; OQ-PF-45; Detailed Rules PF-34 / PF-G9
findings.finding: AC-PF-12 mixes pre-cap and post-cap figures, and the zoom toggle is still there. (1) AC-PF-12 and the Derived-constraints row both report 0.0725 at 640x360 k = 3 against a 0.05 'after the cap' bound, then carve out an exemption. After the cap evaluates to 0 breathing gleams the remaining sum is (353.4 + 120) x 0.291 / 2844 = 0.0484, which is at most 0.05. The exemption is unnecessary and the assertion (r) as worded would fail boot at defaults. (2) On a 640x360 window at stage 3 with the rim, N_G_REGION = 0, so a static-pair lie takes the honest path with filter_draws_dropped when the player zooms in to k = 3 and returns when they zoom out. Zoom is therefore a lie detector, which conflicts with PF-G9 and the user's zoom in/out ruling.
findings.fix: (1) State the post-cap value 0.0484 in AC-PF-12 and in the Derived-constraints row, report 0.0725 as 'pre-cap, not asserted', and drop the exemption clause. (2) Do not tie the honest-path fallback to the current k. findings.section: Sibling sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md SN-23 (L357) and Interactions (L1569) vs Filter PF-15 / PF-37 / AC-PF-93

findings.fix: Under G1 the Filter owns the draw. In Sanity L357 and L1569, replace 'rng_derive keyed filter.leak/...' with 'a Filter-owned presentation hash draw (Perception Filter D.14 tag 7, keyed on the saved lie_id); no kernel stream, no counter, no ledger field'. findings.section: Open Questions OQ-PF-38 item 3; sibling Sanity SN-23 gate (b) (L357)
findings.finding: Sanity's zone-edge eligibility gate is a flat 'zone-edge distance + m_z <= D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000' (400 pm). The Filter can only deliver min(400, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg) = 200 pm at L_s 40 s and 240 deg (D.2: D_eff = min(96, 48) deg). A FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL lie whose zone is 201-400 pm away on a 40-60 s life passes Sanity's gate and then stops short, giving lies_zone_missed. findings.section: Formulas D.3 (the s latch) and AC-PF-120
findings.finding: If a record holds more than one alarm interval, A is chosen as the interval whose nearest edge is closest to the live u_true at the latch frame (the first listed frame or hard_start). findings.section: Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-75c; Detailed Rules PF-18 'Honest-swap accounting'; D.9; OQ-PF-44; sibling hud-and-suit-layer.md HS L316 (GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS)
findings.finding: AC-PF-75c cannot pass at the STRICT default, and this is carried for a third review. The AC says: 'the sum of lying and honest transitions in any rolling second is at most 3, every honest swap that the window cannot hold is skipped to its next grid boundary by the HUD arbiter'. The HUD's rule constant GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1 ('a boundary is never skipped twice in a row ... admitted and counted whatever waits') forces an admission about once per second. At N_r = 3 the lying ticks already run at 2.994/s. Some rolling second therefore holds 4 transitions and the AC's own sum bound fails. The HUD records HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN and leaves it as an ASK to the Filter. OQ-PF-44 'Accept' does not close it.
findings.fix: Rewrite the AC to the achievable oracle. GIVEN STRICT, N_r = 3 lying readouts plus 1 honest numeral in one region, over 60 s: (a) lying ticks 334 +- 1 ms apart, never deferred; (b) the HUD skips at most 1 consecutive honest boundary (GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1), so honest swaps appear at least every 1000 ms; (c) the rolling-second total is at most 3 on every window with no honest swap, and on windows that contain a forced honest swap it is at most 4, each logged as HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN; (d) under the weighted unit ceil(n/2) every window is at most 3. Alternatively cap N_r at 2 in STRICT. Record the choice in OQ-PF-44 and in the HUD's AC-HS-140/141.

The Filter forbids rng_derive (D.14: 'Never rng_derive'; AC-PF-93 lints the source for it) and uses the PRESENTATION hash test against MODE_DROP_PM (tag 7). It is dormant, since MODE_DROP_PM is 0 at MVP, but the two GDDs give opposite implementation instructions. This is carried for a second pass; Sanity was not edited for it.
findings.fix: Under G1 the Filter owns the draw. In Sanity L357 and L1569, replace 'rng_derive keyed filter.leak/...' with 'a Filter-owned presentation hash draw (Perception Filter D.14 tag 7, keyed on the saved lie_id); no kernel stream, no counter, no ledger field'. Drop the 'proposed registry stream' wording.

findings.section: Open Questions OQ-PF-38 item 3; sibling Sanity SN-23 gate (b) (L357)
findings.finding: Sanity's zone-edge eligibility gate is a flat 'zone-edge distance + m_z <= D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000' (400 pm). The Filter can only deliver min(400, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg) = 200 pm at L_s 40 s and 240 deg (D.2: D_eff = min(96, 48) deg). A FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL lie whose zone is 201-400 pm away on a 40-60 s life passes Sanity's gate and then stops short, giving lies_zone_missed. The Filter's own AC-PF-81 labels such a lie 'a weak lie that Sanity's gate should have refused'. OQ-PF-38 still says 'provisional contract until the Filter confirms the constants', but the Filter confirmed them and the derived reach was never handed over.
findings.fix: Edit Sanity gate (b) to use the Filter's published reach: zone-edge distance + m_z <= min(D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg) (200 pm at 40 s, 400 pm from 80 s), with L_s known at the accept. Have the Filter expose reach_pm(L_s, arc_deg) as a pure helper. Then remove the 'provisional' wording in OQ-PF-38 item 3 and add a Sanity AC: a 40 s FALSE_OK whose zone is 250 pm away is refused without a draw.

findings.section: Sibling hud-and-suit-layer.md (HS-28 L257, L1666, AC-HS-104 L1815) and in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md (L398, L985-L998); Open Questions OQ-PF-42
findings.finding: RM_GLIDE_SCALE is still 0.6 in both siblings, against the owner value 0.7 (registry reduced_motion_glide_pm default 700, range 700-1000; Filter L691, L1301). HUD HS-28 and L1666 say '0.6 ... unregistered ... range 0.5-1.0'. AC-HS-104 expects a 2.0 deg/s glide to drop to 1.2 deg/s, but the correct value is 1.4 deg/s, so the test would fail a correct build. Instruments' reduced-motion lint (T_digit / 0.6, 'P 3.05 + 1.34 s') uses the stale divisor; the true figure is smaller, so the lint stays conservative but its worked numbers are wrong. OQ-PF-42 still says 'this GDD edits none of them', which is out of date under G6, and 'HUD has no tremor_weight_pm or BREATH', which is moot for the HUD (it states no tremor on suit readings).
findings.fix: Under G1 the Filter wins. HUD: change 0.6 to 0.7 (registered, range 0.7-1.0, PF-39) at HS-28, L1666 and AC-HS-104 (expected 1.4 deg/s). Instruments: replace 0.6 with 0.7 and recompute the P and p_o2 reduced-motion sums. Close OQ-PF-42 in the Filter, noting that HUD needs neither tremor_weight_pm nor BREATH. After the edits, grep referenced_by documents for RM_GLIDE_SCALE, as the project's consistency-check rule requires.

findings.section: Formulas D.3 (the s latch) and AC-PF-120
findings.finding: If a record holds more than one alarm interval, A is chosen as the interval whose nearest edge is closest to the live u_true at the latch frame (the first listed frame or hard_start). So s depends on live truth and is not restore-exact, yet AC-PF-120 asserts 's is identical after a save/restore'. It is dormant at MVP (dials hold one alarm interval) but the AC is not true for a lie_targets row with two.
findings.fix: Choose A from the static record only, for example the alarm interval nearest mid(OK), so s = d x sgn(mid(OK) - mid(A)) is a function of the entry and the record. Or scope AC-PF-120 to single-alarm records and add a build assertion that MVP records have exactly one.

SN-16's lit-entry rule)', but L279-L285 now define the join on {stable_id, surface} with the IW-8 record. The I-A/I-B intro (L579) still says 'no GDD file existed when this GDD was written ... findings.section: Edge Cases E-PF-57 (L1244), Formulas D.6 rm row (L848), Cross-References X-3 header (L1788)

data.summary: Verdict: APPROVED with 0 BLOCKING, 9 RECOMMENDED and 4 NICE findings. Both pass-3 blockers (the 'away' listing / end-of-lie signature, and conformance to Sanity's SN-23 entry schema) are fully resolved. The G3 stale-wording sweep for hash-key, direction and numeral-mode wording is clean, and Sanity's reach_lie_active, reach_tier and AC-SN-151 hand-off are consistent with the Filter. I recomputed the hash vectors and the arithmetic of D.1-D.17 and the AC vectors against registry defaults; all hold. The work since the last review did not touch this file's carried recommendations, so the same items remain open (the exact ones are in the findings). Three need action before the next story pass: (1) the gleam rise on a truth step contradicts the 'only discontinuity' claim and creates a 'truth just moved' oracle; (2) off-screen / away re-entry (hard_start resets a_env and breath phase) can step the sound LEVEL and breaks the 'identical capture' ACs; (3) AC-PF-75c is unpassable against the HUD's GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1 at N_r 3 in STRICT mode. The rest are sibling conformance (Sanity rng_derive wording, Sanity flat 400 pm zone gate, HUD and Instruments RM_GLIDE_SCALE 0.6 vs 0.7) and stale text. The fixes are local.
